24.0.big: An animal's body shape, tissues and internal controls are all built around one job: staying alive and stable in its environment.
points: This chapter covers body plans, the four basic tissue types, and homeostasis: how the body keeps its insides steady.

24.1.big: An animal's size and shape are limited by physics (support, diffusion, heat), and its energy needs depend on its size and lifestyle.
points: Symmetry: asymmetrical (no pattern, like sponges), radial (like a pie, as in jellyfish; good for catching food from every side), bilateral (left and right mirror halves, like us).
Exoskeletons (chitin) limit size: double the body length and weight goes up about 8×, so the shell would have to get far too thick. Muscles attach to inward bumps called apodemes.
Fast swimmers (sharks, dolphins) have a fusiform shape: tapered at both ends to cut through water.
Diffusion only works over short distances, so big animals need lungs, circulation and folded surfaces.
Endotherms (birds, mammals) make their own body heat and stay at a constant temperature. Ectotherms (reptiles, fish) take heat from the environment.

Metabolic rate: BMR (basal metabolic rate) for endotherms at rest, SMR (standard metabolic rate) for ectotherms. Small animals have more surface area per gram, lose heat faster, and need more energy per gram.
Saving energy: torpor (a short drop in body temperature and activity, like hummingbirds at night), hibernation (long winter torpor), estivation (summer torpor in heat and drought).

Body planes: sagittal (left/right), midsagittal (exactly down the middle), frontal (coronal) (front/back, i.e. ventral/dorsal), transverse (top/bottom). Cavities: the dorsal cavity (brain, spinal cord) and the ventral cavity (thoracic: heart and lungs; abdominal: digestive organs).
24.1.tip: Smaller animal = more surface for its size = loses heat faster = has to eat more for its size.

24.2.big: Animals are made of four tissue types: epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous.
points: Epithelial tissue covers and lines surfaces. Shapes: squamous (flat, good for diffusion, like air sacs), cuboidal (cubes, for secretion), columnar (tall, for absorption, like the intestine), transitional (stretchy, like the bladder).
Layers: simple (one layer), stratified (many layers, for protection like skin), pseudostratified (looks layered but isn't).

Connective tissue = cells spread out in a matrix. Types: loose (areolar) (packing material), fibrous (tendons, ligaments), cartilage (made by chondrocytes, no blood vessels), bone, adipose (fat), and blood (matrix = plasma).

Bone: compact bone is built from osteons. Cells sit in small spaces (lacunae) linked by tiny channels (canaliculi). Spongy bone has struts called trabeculae. Osteoclasts break bone down to release calcium.
Muscle: smooth (involuntary, in organs), skeletal (voluntary, moves bones, striped), cardiac (heart, striped, linked by intercalated discs that pass signals cell to cell).
Nervous: neurons (dendrites receive, the cell body holds the nucleus, the axon sends) plus support cells. Myelin speeds up signals.

24.3.big: Homeostasis keeps your body's conditions (temperature, glucose, calcium) in a safe range, mostly through negative feedback.
points: Every loop has a sensor (receptor), a control center (often the brain), and an effector (a muscle or gland) that makes the change.
A set point is the target value (like 37 °C or about 5 mmol/L of blood glucose). The body stays in a range around it (dynamic equilibrium).
Negative feedback loop = reverse the change. High blood sugar → insulin → sugar goes down. Low calcium → parathyroid hormone (PTH) → calcium goes up.
Positive feedback loop = amplify the change until an endpoint. Childbirth: pressure → oxytocin → stronger contractions → more oxytocin. Blood clotting works the same way. Rare in the body.
An alteration changes the set point (like a fever). Acclimatization is adjusting to a new environment (like high altitude).

Thermoregulation: hot → vasodilation (blood to the skin) and sweating. Cold → vasoconstriction, shivering and insulation. Heat moves by conduction (touch), convection (air or water flow), radiation, and evaporation. The hypothalamus is the thermostat.
24.3.tip: Negative feedback = thermostat (back to normal). Positive feedback = snowball (keeps growing until done).
